1.note: See how you translated this phrase in 1:13

2.note: Solomon is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [There is a time to give birth and a time to die]

The expression **what was planted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [what they planted]

8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **war**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [fighting]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [living peacefully]

9.note: Solomon is using the question form to emphasize that there is no profit for the worker. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [There is no profit for the one who does in exchange for that which he is toiling.]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **profit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [gains]

10.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **business**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [tasks]
See how you translated this phrase in 1:13.

11.q: גַּ֤ם אֶת הָ⁠עֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּ⁠לִבָּ֔⁠ם מִ⁠בְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא יִמְצָ֣א הָ⁠אָדָ֗ם אֶת הַֽ⁠מַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה הָ⁠אֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵ⁠רֹ֥אשׁ וְ⁠עַד סֽוֹף
11.note: Here the word **yet** introduces the result of God giving the sense of duration **in their heart**: **humanity cannot find the work that the God does from beginning to end**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **perpetuity**, you could express the same idea in another way.

Here Solomon is speaking as if the inner being of a person were **their heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in their inner being]
The pronoun **their** refers to the sons of humanity mentioned in 3:10. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the hearts of humanity]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of work, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the deeds]

Solomon is referring to all of God’s work in its entirety by naming two major components, **beginning** and **end**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the very beginning to the very end of everything]

12.q: אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑⁠ם & אִם־לִ⁠שְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְ⁠לַ⁠עֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב
12.note: If it would appear in your language that the Teacher was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [the best thing for them is to rejoice and to do good]
The pronoun **his** refers to each person among those the Teacher has been discussing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [during their lives]

13.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **toil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [his hard work]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **gift**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is a gracious act of]

14.q: עָלָי⁠ו֙ אֵ֣ין לְ⁠הוֹסִ֔יף וּ⁠מִמֶּ֖⁠נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִ⁠גְרֹ֑עַ
14.note: Qoheleth is referring to all possible changes by naming two major components, **nothing to add** and **nothing to remove**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language.
Here, **his face** represents his presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from before his presence]

15.note: Qoheleth is using **God seeks that which is pursued** as a common expression of the culture to mean “God calls back the past.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the God calls back what has passed away]

The expression **is pursued** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that which people pursue]

16.note: See how you translated this phrase in 1:3.

16.q: מְק֤וֹם הַ⁠מִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּ⁠ה הָ⁠רֶ֔שַׁע וּ⁠מְק֥וֹם הַ⁠צֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּ⁠ה הָ⁠רָֽשַׁע
16.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way.

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **justice**, **wickedness**, and **equity**, you could express these same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [just decisions—there was wicked deeds, and the place of righteous actions—there was wicked deeds]

17.note: Solomon is using **I said, I in my heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I thought to myself.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly.
If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [That God will judge both the righteous and the wicked]

18.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:17.

18.q: עַל דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָ⁠אָדָ֔ם לְ⁠בָרָ֖⁠ם הָ⁠אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְ⁠לִ⁠רְא֕וֹת שְׁ⁠הֶם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָ⁠הֶֽם
18.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [that God tests the sons of humanity to show that they themselves are animals]
See how you translated the same phrase in 1:13.

Here Solomon is speaking as if human beings were animals. He means that in terms of mortality, humans are no different from animals. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that they themselves are no different from animals]

The pronoun they themselves refers to the sons of humanity. Solomon uses the independent pronoun for emphasis. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the sons of humanity themselves]

19.q: כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־הָ⁠אָדָ֜ם וּ⁠מִקְרֶ֣ה הַ⁠בְּהֵמָ֗ה וּ⁠מִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָ⁠הֶ֔ם
19.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of happening, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For what happens to the sons of humanity and what happens to the animal—and what happens is for them both]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:13.
The first use of the pronoun **this one** refers to a human being, and the second use refers to an animal. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of advantage, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [But the way that humanity is better than the animal]
See how you translated this expression in 1:14.

20.note: Qoheleth is referring to death in a polite way by using the phrase going to one place. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [Both are going to the grave]

20.q: הַ⁠כֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־הֶֽ⁠עָפָ֔ר וְ⁠הַ⁠כֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־הֶ⁠עָפָֽר
20.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if people and animals were made from the dust and will become dust again. He is alluding to the way God created the first human being out of the ground. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Both were made from dirt, and both will turn back into dirt]

21.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to express that no one can know for certain what happens after death. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [No one can know for sure.]
See how you translated this expression in 1:13.

22.note: The pronoun **his** refers to humanity collectively, spoken of as a single person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [each person should rejoice in his works]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the enjoyment of work were a **portion** of food allotted to someone. He means that it is what God has assigned to each person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it is what God has assigned to him]

22.q: כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֨⁠נּוּ֙ לִ⁠רְא֔וֹת בְּ⁠מֶ֖ה שֶׁ⁠יִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽי⁠ו
22.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one can show a person what will happen after him. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For no one can show him what will happen after him]
